plan.title: Confounded lung treated vs control DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The design has 6 treated vs 6 control lung samples, but batch B1 holds all controls and B2 holds all treated samples — batch and condition are perfectly confounded (rank-deficient if both are modeled). Per R-0005, no batch term, ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, or SV-based correction can be applied without also removing the condition effect; the only valid path is to fit condition alone under the explicit assumption that no batch effect exists, and to label every downstream result as confounded rather than a clean causal finding. The plan: (1) QC on the raw salmon-derived counts to visualize whether PC1 tracks condition/batch (which here are identical, so this step documents rather than resolves the confound), (2) minimal pre-filter and DESeq2 Wald test with design ~condition (reference level = control), apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05, (3) fgsea preranked enrichment on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways (human) gene sets, and (4) a report that states the confound explicitly in every section and frames results as hypothesis-generating only. Counts are gene-level from salmon with no stated length correction (import_state unknown), so the model runs on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and this limitation is stated in the report.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If the batch is perfectly confounded with the condition, do not fit a batch term and do not adjust the counts with ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, or a surrogate variable method. The model matrix is not full rank, and a removal method would remove the condition effect with the batch. State the assumption of no batch effect and label every result as confounded, or stop and ask for a design where the batches hold every condition.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
